name: li_fat_id first party click ID
plain: A click ID added to ad landing page URLs and saved as a first party cookie.
meaning: Survives third party cookie blocking and lets the advertiser's tag and API tie a later purchase to a LinkedIn ad click and member.

web.api: ?li_fat_id=<uuid> on landing URL; cookie li_fat_id; firstPartyTrackingEnabled on the tag

access.persistence: Cookie 30 days from latest ad click; member mapping stored 365 days
steps: Enhanced conversion tracking is on (default for new tags)
LinkedIn appends li_fat_id to the ad's landing URL
Insight Tag writes it to a first party cookie
Value is sent in Insight Tag events and in the Conversions API as LINKEDIN_FIRST_PARTY_ADS_TRACKING_UUID

limits.headline: Can tag your visit from a LinkedIn ad click with an ID the site saves
limits.user_action: You click a LinkedIn ad and land on the advertiser's page
can: Add a click ID to the ad link's web address
Save that ID as a cookie on the advertiser's own site
Match a later purchase or sign up back to your ad click
cannot: Exist unless you arrived by clicking a LinkedIn ad link
Follow you to other sites, since it is saved only on the advertiser's site
Work after you clear cookies or if the browser removes the ID
Identify you by name; it is a code linked to the click
limits.reach_label: One ad click, kept for weeks
limits.differs: Some browsers strip known click IDs from links, which cuts this off.

story.what_it_is: A click code in LinkedIn ad links, saved as a cookie to tie later actions to that click.

marketing.name: First party cookies
marketing.pitch: LinkedIn describes first party cookie tracking as a way to keep conversion measurement working with fewer third party cookies.

story.for_you: You click a LinkedIn ad and the web address has a long code in it. The site saves that code in its own cookie, so a purchase a week later can be linked back to your click.
story.for_makers: Third party cookies are fading, so advertisers need another way to prove an ad worked. A click code saved on the advertiser's own domain survives most blockers. It also lets the advertiser send the code back by server for a more complete count.

use_cases.example: You click a LinkedIn ad for project software, sign up days later, and the vendor ties the signup to that ad.
A marketing team sees the whole path from ad click to demo to deal, even when the sale takes months.
A business buys office chairs after clicking an ad, and the shop credits the sale to LinkedIn.
A sales system stores the click code with a lead, so reps can see which ad created each lead.
Safari and Firefox limit such cookies or strip known click codes, so some clicks are never matched.
A podcast sponsor tracks signups from a LinkedIn promoted post to decide next quarter budget.

risks: Follows a click to a later purchase

technical_bounds: Only set for people who arrive from a LinkedIn ad
Can be stripped by link cleaning (Safari, Brave, Firefox Strict)

legit_uses: Attribute conversions without third party cookies

linkedin.how: Documented by Microsoft Learn enabling-first-party-cookies page.
